proposals.old: Wood v. Lucy implied the reasonable-efforts duty; § 205 states a general duty of good faith in performance for every contract.
proposals.new: Wood v. Lucy implied a reasonable-efforts promise that supplied consideration. Section 205 later states the distinct general duty of good faith in performance and enforcement.
proposals.reason: Implied reasonable efforts supporting consideration and the later performance/enforcement duty are related but distinct inquiries; avoid calling section 205 a codification of this precise holding.

proposals.old: RLCC § 6 restates unconscionability for consumer contracts in the same shape.
proposals.new: Consumer Restatement § 6 supplies a consumer-specific sliding-scale test and specified examples. UCC § 2-302 grants enforcement remedies without defining the substantive test.
proposals.reason: The consumer formulation expressly specifies a sliding scale and possible sufficiency of one factor; it is not identical to the UCC provision.

proposals.old: Section 1-303 defines usage of trade and ranks it below express terms, course of performance and course of dealing.
proposals.new: Section 1-303 defines trade usage and supplies a hierarchy when terms cannot reasonably be reconciled. Course of performance may also show waiver or modification, subject to § 2-209.
proposals.reason: Retain the reasonable-consistency condition and subsection (f) waiver/modification exception to a categorical hierarchy.

proposals.old: Columbia Nitrogen read a usage of trade into a written price term under §§ 1-205 and 2-202.
proposals.new: Columbia Nitrogen required admission of usage and dealing evidence to explain or supplement the writing under former §§ 1-205 and 2-202, subject to reasonable consistency. It ordered retrial rather than deciding that the buyer owed nothing.
proposals.reason: Distinguish admission and retrial from a final finding that usage altered a price obligation; both price and quantity were disputed.
